finding.claim: The purge handler calls checkPerm(u, "admin") but discards the boolean result, so the admin check is never enforced. Any caller who reaches the route can run the destructive purgeAll(). The sibling handler rotateKeys correctly uses mustPerm and returns on failure.
finding.source: Any authenticated (or otherwise able to reach the route) HTTP user without the admin permission sends a request to the purge handler.
finding.sink: purgeAll() at handlers.go:27, the admin-only destructive operation.

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) loads the user from the request context
checkPerm(u, "admin") returns a bool that is ignored, so there is no early return or 403
Contrast: rotateKeys uses if !mustPerm(...) { return }, which is the correct pattern

finding.guards_checked: Searched the only source file (handlers.go) for middleware or route registration that might enforce admin before purge. None exists in this directory. userFrom only fetches the user and does no authorization. checkPerm only returns a value and does not write a response. Route wiring and auth middleware are not present in the repo, so a global admin guard outside this code cannot be ruled out.

verdict.reason: handlers.go:26 calls checkPerm(u, "admin"), which only returns u.Perms[perm] (handlers.go:12-14) and never writes a response. The result is discarded, so purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any caller who reaches the route. The sibling rotateKeys correctly uses mustPerm and returns on failure (handlers.go:33-35). No route wiring or middleware exists in the repo, so an external global guard can't be ruled out, but nothing in the code blocks it.
